analyzed.function: Raffle._update (override) reached via inherited ERC721 transferFrom / safeTransferFrom (x2) / _safeMint->_mint / _burn

trustBoundaries.reaches: Calls quoteToken.decimals() in try/catch, then new Raffle, whose VRF consumer-base constructor calls wrapper.link() (VCB L45). Fixes quoteToken, vrfWrapper, protocolTreasury and raffleImplementation for every clone. The treasury is screened only against the factory, quote token, wrapper and implementation (RF L80, L90), never against future clone CREATE addresses. No powers after deployment.

Deploys clone k at factory nonce k+1 (CREATE). Runs Raffle.initialize (factory-only), which screens sponsor, treasury and recipient through the factory getters. Writes the registry (isRaffle becomes true at RF L125, before escrow). Then hands control to the sponsor-chosen prize contract at RF L128 (W1) while the new clone is registered, unguarded and, after L428, Active. Ends with the prize contract's own ownerOf answer (RF L129) and a status()==Active check (RF L132).

trustBoundaries.entrypoint: Raffle.enableRefunds, untimed path for a raffle with no sales (L282)
trustBoundaries.reaches: Moves Active to Refunding with zero liability at any time while totalEntries==0. This overlaps the sale window and closes after any purchase. Opens releaseSponsorPrize. Reachable inside W1 only through a contract sponsor; there, RF L132 then reverts the creation.

trustBoundaries.entrypoint: Raffle.onERC721Received (L416-L431), with the prize contract as msg.sender; the prize contract is itself called at RF L172/L128/L129 and Raffle L334/L335, L404/L405
trustBoundaries.reaches: Is the only writer of Active (L428), based on (operator, from, tokenId) values it supplies itself. Answers every custody check (RF L129, L335, L405). In W1 it can call buyEntries, the ticket ERC-721 functions, other clones and the factory getters on an Active clone whose guard is open. In W6 and W10 it can reach only unguarded clone functions. Its acceptance decides whether the only NftWon NFT exit (L334) and the CashWon/Refunding exit (L404) succeed.

USDC transferFrom of n·1e6 (trusted token; nominal amount, no balance check). Writes the range, counters and pot. Mints the ticket through _safeMint, whose _update screen makes factory STATICCALLs. Calls the recipient's onERC721Received with the clone guard held (W3). Any payer, including the sponsor, the sponsorRecipient or the treasury, can push totalEntries toward reserveEntries.

trustBoundaries.entrypoint: onERC721Received callbacks from _safeMint (E L289) and from ticket safeTransferFrom (E L135)
trustBoundaries.reaches: In W3 (guard held): ticket transfers and approvals, other clones, and createRaffle. In W11 from a top-level transfer (guard not held): every clone function, acting as the new owner, including refundTickets and redeemWinningTicket inside the callback.

Burns tickets, debits the liability (checked) and pays USDC to msg.sender (screened at L565). Can trigger inline settlement. NFT delivery goes through prize.transferFrom, and the only delivery evidence is the prize contract's ownerOf answer (W6). No deadline applies.

trustBoundaries.entrypoint: Inherited ERC-721 transferFrom, safeTransferFrom (x2), approve, setApprovalForAll (E L93-L136)
trustBoundaries.reaches: Can move tickets in every status to any address that passes the point-in-time screen, including themselves, and then claim as owner. Approval targets are never screened. Operator approvals are keyed per owner and survive transfers.

Moves Active to Drawing. Makes wrapper quote STATICCALLs, then calls requestRandomWordsInNative with value taken only from msg.value (W4, with _requestInFlight set). Receives a full-gas native refund CALL (W5) after status=Drawing and vrfRequestId are set and _requestInFlight is cleared. Chooses the tx.gasprice that prices the request.

trustBoundaries.actor: Chainlink VRF v2.5 wrapper (trusted; identity set by the deployer)
trustBoundaries.reaches: Is the only writer of NftWon, CashWon, winningEntry and resolvedAt; the call has no guard. A callback resolves only if not in flight, status is Drawing, the ID matches, exactly one word is delivered and t < drawRequestedAt+2d. Otherwise it emits VrfCallbackIgnored. The word alone selects the winning entry (word % n + 1).

trustBoundaries.entrypoint: enableRefunds (after deadlines), settleWinningTicket, releaseSponsorProceeds, releaseProtocolFees, releaseSponsorPrize
trustBoundaries.reaches: Move status to Refunding after deadlines. Settle in storage only, with a ticket ID that has exactly one valid value. Pay USDC to the fixed sponsorRecipient and protocolTreasury (screened at payout). Send the prize NFT to the fixed sponsorRecipient through the prize contract (W10; no screen at release). Keepers choose timing only, never destinations.

trustBoundaries.entrypoint: Receives USDC at L380 and the NFT at L404
trustBoundaries.reaches: Screened at creation only (RF L163-L169, L193). USDC is screened again at every release (L565); the NFT is not. Plain transferFrom gives it no receiver hook. A code-less future clone CREATE address passes the creation screen.
Screened in the factory constructor against addresses that exist at construction, and in each initialize (L190, which includes the new clone address). Screened again at each release (L565).
Moves all value; the clone's balance is never read. L224 runs before the purchase's own writes, with the guard held. Issuer controls can make any payout revert, including to fixed payees.

trustBoundaries.actor: RaffleFactory registry (trusted), as consulted by clones
trustBoundaries.reaches: Defines the denylist for every clone. Grows at each createRaffle, which is callable from any clone's untrusted window except W1. Includes the in-flight clone during W1. The getters have no guard.

trustBoundaries.actor: Anyone (deployers of third-party proxies, direct callers of the implementation)
trustBoundaries.reaches: The implementation is locked (Refunding, initialized) and every mutator reverts; setApprovalForAll writes only to its own storage. Third-party proxies can never be initialized (L178), stay AwaitingPrize with prizeToken 0, are not registered and are not denylist members.

See flags and events that can come before custody or differ from final ownership: isRaffle true during W1, TicketPurchased before RaffleCreated, TicketPurchased.recipient different from the owner, prizeClaimed/winnerRedeemed true before delivery, and RaffleResolved before DrawRequested if a callback lands in W5.

fragilityClusters.area: Prize custody self-reported by the prize contract: RaffleFactory.createRaffle RF L127-L134, Raffle.onERC721Received L416-L431, redeemWinningTicket L329-L337, releaseSponsorPrize L395-L407
fragilityClusters.why: The sponsor-chosen contract answers every custody check: escrow acceptance (arguments it supplies), the escrow check (RF L129) and both delivery checks (L335, L405). Nothing observes custody independently. IRaffle NatSpec (honest prizes) and DESIGN.md (untrusted prizes) disagree. In NftWon, one external transferFrom is the only NFT exit, while the sponsor's 95% and the treasury's 5% are released independently.

Between Raffle L428 (Active) and RF L129-L132, the new clone is already registered (isRaffle true) and Active, with its guard open, while sponsor-chosen code runs. buyEntries, ticket transfers and approvals, and a sponsor-driven enableRefunds are reachable. RF L132 checks only status, so purchases survive, and TicketPurchased logs come before RaffleCreated.

fragilityClusters.area: Point-in-time destination screening: Raffle._isProtocolDestination L593-L605 with callers L187-L195, L498, L565; unscreened outflows L334, L404, L267 and approvals
fragilityClusters.why: Each outflow is screened at a different moment. The result can flip from false to true only for code-less future CREATE addresses, which are computable because raffleById[k] = CREATE(factory, k+1). The screen covers only same-factory plumbing (not LINK, the coordinator, other factories' clones, third-party proxies, or other raffles' prizes). USDC to sponsorRecipient is screened again at release, but the NFT is not. A treasury equal to a future clone address halts creation at that nonce permanently.

fragilityClusters.area: VRF request/callback boundary: requestDraw L240-L273, fulfillRandomWords L509-L524, VCB L76-L107
fragilityClusters.why: _requestInFlight covers only the wrapper call (W4). The full-gas native refund to msg.sender (W5) runs after status=Drawing and vrfRequestId are set. It is the one point where Raffle code does not exclude an unguarded state writer (rawFulfillRandomWords) running inside a guarded frame. Request-ID semantics, routing, re-delivery, gas forwarding, value returned by the wrapper, configuration bounds and caller-chosen gas price all depend on wrapper code that is not vendored. Time boundaries at L512/L291 are exact complements.

fragilityClusters.area: Terminal-state claim decoupling: settleWinningTicket/_settleWinningTicket L304-L306/L533-L558, redeemWinningTicket L309-L346, releaseSponsorProceeds L375-L382, releaseProtocolFees L385-L392, releaseSponsorPrize L395-L407
fragilityClusters.why: Settlement is permissionless and touches only storage, so sponsor and treasury USDC become releasable whether or not the winner's delivery succeeds. Redemption is a bearer claim with no deadline and no alternative claimant: one NFT exit in NftWon, one consumer of winnerProceeds in CashWon. One-shot flags shared across functions are separated only by status, and they read true before the prize contract runs.

fragilityClusters.area: Nominal USDC accounting: buyEntries L223-L233, enableRefunds L296-L298, refundTickets L363-L369, _settleWinningTicket L539-L555, _transferQuote L564-L567
fragilityClusters.why: Every amount is ENTRY_PRICE × entries, and src never reads balanceOf. Solvency rests on USDC being fee-free and non-rebasing, and on issuer controls (pause, blocklist) not applying. Those controls can block fixed payees or holders. Unclaimed liabilities and unsolicited surplus have no sweep and no deadline.

fragilityClusters.area: Unguarded ERC-721 ticket surface and receiver callbacks: E L93-L136 via Raffle._update L497-L502; mint hook R L235 → E L289
fragilityClusters.why: Tickets move in every lifecycle status; there is no status gate. Hooks from top-level safeTransferFrom run with the clone guard not entered, so a new owner can refund or redeem inside the callback. Operator approvals persist per owner. Raffle reads ownership only at L320 and L359, each followed immediately by a burn. TicketPurchased.recipient can differ from the owner when the call returns.

fragilityClusters.area: Timeline hand-offs and keeper dependence: buyEntries L216, requestDraw L242-L247, enableRefunds L276-L301, drawRequestDeadline/callbackDeadline L458-L465, fulfillRandomWords L512
fragilityClusters.why: Each of three hand-offs uses one deadline function on both sides. The sponsor's untimed exit for a raffle with no sales overlaps the sale window and is separated only by state. Nothing transitions automatically and there is no incentive to call, so refunds and the prize return wait for someone to call enableRefunds. Terminal states have no deadlines. Block-producer timestamps decide which side a boundary block lands on.

fragilityClusters.area: Creation-time validation split between RaffleFactory._validateCreateParams RF L154-L179 and Raffle.initialize L176-L206
fragilityClusters.why: Different checks live in different contracts: the sponsor checks, treasury-vs-prize, recipient-vs-new-clone, and the code-gated isRaffle query are in initialize only. Admission accepts raffle tickets from other factory deployments as prizes, since it excludes only same-factory clones. reserveEntries has no upper bound. The clone stores the factory-validated parameters without rechecking them.

unenforcedAssumptions: Raffle.redeemWinningTicket: prizeToken.transferFrom(clone, winner, prizeTokenId) actually moves the escrowed NFT to winner.
Raffle.redeemWinningTicket: prizeToken.ownerOf reports custody truthfully. The L335 delivery check is answered by the same untrusted contract that did the transfer.

Raffle.redeemWinningTicket: The prize contract does not revert, exhaust gas, or restrict a transfer from the clone to the winner. In NftWon there is no other way out for the NFT and no redemption deadline.
Raffle.redeemWinningTicket: The clone still owns the prize NFT at redemption time.
Raffle.redeemWinningTicket: The clone's USDC balance is at least winnerProceeds at L342.
Raffle.redeemWinningTicket: quoteToken.transfer to winner succeeds (no issuer blocklist or pause). On failure every effect reverts and the ticket stays transferable.
Raffle.redeemWinningTicket: In NftWon, the sponsor's 95% and the treasury's 5% are released only after the winner receives the NFT.
Raffle.redeemWinningTicket: External readers do not treat winnerRedeemed, prizeClaimed or winnerRecipient as proof of delivery while L334 is running.
Raffle._settleWinningTicket: The clone actually holds at least grossPot USDC, so the allocations can be paid.
Raffle._settleWinningTicket: status correctly selects 95/5 vs 80/15/5, and the sponsor-chosen reserveEntries has an upper bound.
Raffle.buyEntries: USDC transferFrom delivers exactly grossAmount to the clone (fee-free, non-rebasing).
Raffle.buyEntries: USDC transferFrom makes no callback into the payer, the recipient or the clone.
Raffle.buyEntries: The recipient can later act on the ticket (refund, redeem or transfer it).
Raffle.buyEntries: A recipient's protocol-destination status does not change after mint.
Raffle.refundTickets: The clone's USDC balance >= remainingRefundLiability, so L369 does not fail for insufficient balance.
Raffle.refundTickets: A non-reverting quoteToken.transfer moved exactly `amount` to msg.sender.
Raffle.refundTickets: The quote token does not refuse the transfer to msg.sender (blacklist, pause).
Raffle.enableRefunds: The clone's USDC balance is at least the liability moved into remainingRefundLiability.
Raffle.enableRefunds: Only the sponsor's own controller can make msg.sender equal sponsor at L282.
Raffle.enableRefunds: Someone calls enableRefunds after the applicable deadline. Refund and prize-return availability (L350, L397) depend on that call.
Raffle.fulfillRandomWords (reached via inherited VRFV2PlusWrapperConsumerBase.rawFulfillRandomWords): i_vrfV2PlusWrapper is the genuine Chainlink VRF v2.5 wrapper for the chain

Raffle.fulfillRandomWords (reached via inherited VRFV2PlusWrapperConsumerBase.rawFulfillRandomWords): The requestId passed to rawFulfillRandomWords equals the ID returned by requestRandomWordsInNative and stored at L259, and IDs are non-zero and unique

Raffle.fulfillRandomWords (reached via inherited VRFV2PlusWrapperConsumerBase.rawFulfillRandomWords): The wrapper routes each callback only to the requesting clone and delivers at most once; an ignored live callback is not re-delivered
Raffle.fulfillRandomWords (reached via inherited VRFV2PlusWrapperConsumerBase.rawFulfillRandomWords): Exactly one word is delivered for the numWords=1 request (L257)
Raffle.fulfillRandomWords (reached via inherited VRFV2PlusWrapperConsumerBase.rawFulfillRandomWords): randomWords[0] is unpredictable before the fulfillment transaction and not chosen by any party

Raffle.fulfillRandomWords (reached via inherited VRFV2PlusWrapperConsumerBase.rawFulfillRandomWords): No matching callback arrives between L260 and the end of requestDraw, where L267 calls the untrusted requester with full gas
Raffle.fulfillRandomWords (reached via inherited VRFV2PlusWrapperConsumerBase.rawFulfillRandomWords): The callback receives enough gas for the fixed-cost body
Raffle.fulfillRandomWords (reached via inherited VRFV2PlusWrapperConsumerBase.rawFulfillRandomWords): uint64(block.timestamp) at L520 does not truncate

Raffle.requestDraw: The requestId returned by the wrapper is non-zero, unique, and is the ID the wrapper will later pass to this clone's rawFulfillRandomWords. IRaffle L100/L484 use 0 to mean 'no request'.

Raffle.requestDraw: No authenticated callback for requestId reaches this clone after L260 in the same transaction, in particular during the L267 call to msg.sender. fulfillRandomWords L510-L513 would accept such a callback, because in-flight is false, status is Drawing, the IDs match and the deadline has not passed.
Raffle.requestDraw: The wrapper keeps exactly requestPrice and sends no native value back to the clone.
Raffle.requestDraw: calculateRequestPriceNative returns the same value at L437 and at VRFV2PlusWrapperConsumerBase.sol L82 within one transaction.

Raffle.requestDraw: The configured wrapper accepts callbackGasLimit 300_000, requestConfirmations 30, numWords 1 and nativePayment extraArgs throughout [endTime, endTime + 2d). If it does not, no draw is possible and only enableRefunds (L285-L288) remains.
Raffle.requestDraw: uint64(block.timestamp) at L253 does not truncate.
Raffle.requestDraw: Enough gas remains after the L267 call to run L269, L272 and the guard reset. If the recipient burns all forwarded gas, only the EIP-150 retained 1/64 is left.
Raffle.requestDraw: msg.sender can accept native value when excess != 0.
RaffleFactory.createRaffle: prize.safeTransferFrom at L128 actually moves prizeTokenId from msg.sender to the clone.
RaffleFactory.createRaffle: ownerOf == clone at L129 reflects real custody that lasts until R L334 or R L404 delivers the prize.
RaffleFactory.createRaffle: supportsInterface(IERC721) == true means the contract follows ERC-721 transfer and ownership semantics.
RaffleFactory.createRaffle: protocolTreasury differs from every clone address this factory will deploy.
RaffleFactory.createRaffle: Contracts reached during L128 do not treat isRaffle(clone) == true as proof that the escrow was verified.
RaffleFactory.createRaffle: The clone has no sold entries when RaffleCreated is emitted.
Raffle.onERC721Received: The (operator, from, tokenId) arguments describe a real transfer of prizeTokenId from sponsor into this clone, made by the factory.
Raffle.onERC721Received: The prize contract is honest and standards-compliant (IRaffle L14-L15, IRaffleFactory L16).
Raffle.onERC721Received: The factory immutable is the RaffleFactory that clones and initializes this raffle and that calls safeTransferFrom, so a conforming prize reports operator == factory.
Raffle.releaseSponsorPrize: The clone owns prizeTokenId on entry.
Raffle.releaseSponsorPrize: prizeToken.transferFrom moves the NFT from the clone to recipient and does nothing else.
Raffle.releaseSponsorPrize: prizeToken.ownerOf reports the true owner.
Raffle.releaseSponsorPrize: sponsorRecipient is not protocol plumbing (this clone, factory, implementation, USDC, VRF wrapper, prize token, or any registered clone of this factory) at release time.
Raffle.releaseSponsorPrize: sponsorRecipient can hold and later move an ERC-721.
Raffle.releaseSponsorPrize: The prize contract accepts a transfer to sponsorRecipient whenever release is attempted (not paused, recipient not blocked, token not locked).

Raffle._update (override) reached via inherited ERC721 transferFrom / safeTransferFrom (x2) / _safeMint->_mint / _burn: An address that passes the screen stays outside the protocol-destination set for as long as it holds the ticket.

Raffle._update (override) reached via inherited ERC721 transferFrom / safeTransferFrom (x2) / _safeMint->_mint / _burn: The screen covers every address whose ownership would make a ticket claim unreachable.
Raffle._update (override) reached via inherited ERC721 transferFrom / safeTransferFrom (x2) / _safeMint->_mint / _burn: TicketPurchased.recipient equals ownerOf(ticketId) when buyEntries returns.

Raffle._update (override) reached via inherited ERC721 transferFrom / safeTransferFrom (x2) / _safeMint->_mint / _burn: A safe-transfer recipient cannot call guarded Raffle functions during its onERC721Received callback.
Raffle._isProtocolDestination: An address that passes the screen now will not later become a registered clone.
Raffle._isProtocolDestination: A ticket owner remains a non-protocol destination after receiving the ticket.
Raffle._isProtocolDestination: sponsorRecipient is still a non-protocol destination when the prize NFT is returned.
Raffle._isProtocolDestination: protocolTreasury is not the address of a future factory clone.
Raffle._isProtocolDestination: The seven predicates cover every protocol-adjacent address that cannot use a ticket or a USDC claim.
unresolved: U-01 Prize trust model [01,03,08,09,10]: Which governs, IRaffle L14-L15 / L40 / IRaffleFactory L16 ('honest, standards-compliant') or DESIGN.md L2 ('arbitrary prize contracts ... untrusted')? On-chain admission checks only for code, excludes plumbing and accepts an ERC-165 self-report; there is no allowlist and there are no tests. The answer decides whether the self-reported ownerOf checks at RF L129, L335 and L405 are the intended custody boundary. It also decides whether transfer-restricted prizes (pausable, blocklisting, transfer validators, upgradeable proxies, soulbound) are in scope; these can block L334 (the only NftWon exit) or L404 permanently.

U-02 USDC on the target chain [01,02,03,04]: Does the deployed USDC proxy and implementation move exactly the nominal amount, with no fee, rebase or hook, in transferFrom (L224) and transfer (L566)? Under which blocklist or pause conditions does it revert or return false? Can that be permanent for a fixed payee (sponsorRecipient, treasury) or a holder (L342, L369)? No USDC source is present and no balanceOf is read.

U-03 Unredeemed winning ticket [01]: Is any off-chain or out-of-scope mechanism expected to handle a winning ticket whose holder never redeems? The code has no deadline and no alternative claimant: L334 is the only NftWon NFT exit (L397), and winnerProceeds has a single consumer.

U-04 Flags and events treated as proof [01,09,10]: Do integrators or indexers treat winnerRedeemed, prizeClaimed, winnerRecipient, PrizeDeposited, RaffleCreated or SponsorPrizeReleased as proof of escrow or delivery? The flags are written before the prize call (L323-L331, L403), and the events rest on the prize contract's own answers (L429, RF L129, L405).
U-05 reserveEntries upper bound [02]: Is an upper bound intended? Only != 0 is enforced (RF L178), so the sponsor decides at creation whether NftWon (L543) can be reached.

U-06 Unreachable ticket holders [03,11]: What is intended for claims whose owner can never call refund or redeem? Examples: code-less addresses nobody controls, contracts with no call path, and CREATE-predicted future clone addresses. buyEntries excludes only zero and the sinks visible at mint (L217, L498-L500, L602). Relatedly, is the code-length gate at L602 meant to let future clone CREATE addresses bypass the registry screen (rationale only at L589)?

U-07 Indexer semantics and selling during creation [03,08,09,11]: How do off-chain consumers (none in the tree) treat TicketPurchased.recipient versus the final owner (L236 is emitted after the W3 hook), TicketPurchased emitted inside the creation window before RaffleCreated, and Transfer logs that precede TicketPurchased? Is selling entries inside RF L128 intended, given that RF L132 reads only status and the sponsor's early-cancel path requires totalEntries == 0?

U-08 EIP-7702 [03,08]: Does the deployment chain support delegation designators? A delegated EOA has non-empty code. It receives ticket hooks (U L32), triggers the isRaffle query (L602) and passes _requireContract as prizeToken (RF L184). Its code can be re-pointed after creation, which affects whether custody lasts.

U-09 VRF fee on abandoned requests [05]: After enableRefunds runs from Drawing, can the outstanding request still be fulfilled later? Is the native fee paid at VCB L84 ever returned? Raffle ignores such callbacks (L511) and has no reimbursement path.

U-10 Keeper operations [05]: Who is expected to call enableRefunds once a deadline passes? There is no incentive or automation, and refundTickets (L350) and releaseSponsorPrize (L397) wait on that call.

U-11 VRF request-ID semantics [06,07]: Does the ID returned by requestRandomWordsInNative (stored unvalidated at L259) equal the ID passed to rawFulfillRandomWords? Is it non-zero, unique across consumers and bound to the requesting clone? Is each callback routed only to the requester, delivered at most once, with array length == numWords (1)?

U-12 Same-transaction callback and re-delivery [06,07]: Can a callback arrive synchronously inside VCB L84, or between L260 and L272? The case that matters most is during the L267 refund call to msg.sender, where L510-L513 would accept it. Is an ignored callback ever re-delivered?
U-13 Callback gas [06]: How does the wrapper forward gas, and how does it handle a consumer revert or out-of-gas? Does the 300_000 limit (RC L39) actually reach the callback body?
U-14 Wrapper administration [06]: Can the wrapper owner disable the wrapper or change its coordinator after a request is accepted, forcing a Drawing raffle onto the refund path?
U-15 Block-timestamp rules [06]: The target chain's timestamp rules decide which side of the L512/L291 boundary a fulfillment lands on, and likewise for L216 and L245/L287.

U-16 Price-quote consistency [07]: Does calculateRequestPriceNative return the same value at L437 and at VCB L82 within one transaction? A divergence changes which InsufficientVrfFee check fires and the size of excess.
U-17 Value sent back by the wrapper [07]: Does the wrapper keep exactly requestPrice, or can it send native value back? The clone's receive() reverts and there is no fallback.

U-18 Wrapper/coordinator configuration bounds [07]: Can the fixed parameters (300_000 gas, 30 confirmations, 1 word, native extraArgs) be rejected for the entire [endTime, endTime+2d) window? That would leave enableRefunds (L285-L288) as the only exit from Active.

U-19 Fulfilment at a caller-chosen gas price [07]: Does the oracle network fulfil requests priced at an arbitrary tx.gasprice (IW L27-L28) within DRAW_CALLBACK_TIMEOUT? Raffle sets no fee floor beyond the wrapper quote (L250, L258).

U-20 Treasury versus future clone addresses [08,12]: How does the deployment tooling (absent from the workspace) choose protocolTreasury_ relative to the factory's future CREATE addresses? The constructor checks only addresses that exist at construction (RF L80, L90). If they are equal, that createRaffle reverts at L190, and because the nonce does not advance, every later one reverts too.

U-21 isRaffle during escrow [08]: Is it intended that isRaffle(newClone) is true throughout RF L128 (RF L125 runs before escrow), given IRaffleFactory L138 says 'True only for a successfully created canonical clone'? Which integrators consult isRaffle?

U-22 Multiple deployments [11,12]: Will other RaffleFactory deployments or Raffle-compatible clones exist on the same chain? Do they count as 'raffle clones' under DESIGN.md L2? The screen recognizes only same-factory clones and the same-factory implementation (L587, L601-L603).

U-23 Prize contract as ticket operator [11]: May the prize contract be approved as a ticket operator? It cannot own a ticket (L600), but approvals are unscreened (E L93-L107), and it executes inside W6/W10, where unguarded ticket transfers remain callable.
U-24 Denylist membership [12]: Were i_linkToken (VCB L45) and the wrapper's coordinator meant to be denylist members? Neither is compared.

U-25 Screening times for sponsorRecipient [10,12]: Why is USDC to sponsorRecipient screened at release (L380 → L565) while the NFT is screened only at initialization (L193 → L402-L404)? Does anything off-chain reject a sponsorRecipient that is an unused future CREATE address of this factory?

U-26 Persistent prize-return failure [10]: What recovery is intended if L404 keeps reverting in CashWon or Refunding? The recipient is write-once (L198), status is terminal, and NatSpec L24-L25 rules out any rescue path.

S-01 (raised in synthesis) Sponsor account type: Are sponsors expected to be EOAs only? A contract sponsor with a path that third parties can call (smart wallet, multisig module, 7702 delegate) would let others use the untimed empty-raffle exit (L282), including from inside the creation window W1 (basis: UA-19, [05], [09] case f).

S-02 (raised in synthesis) Other deployments' tickets as prizes: Clones registered in another RaffleFactory deployment are code-bearing ERC-721s that report IERC721 (E L45-L50), and RF L159 excludes only clones registered in this factory. Is escrowing such tickets intended? Their claims stay dormant until the ticket is delivered (relates to U-22).
S-03 (raised in synthesis) Losing tickets: After resolution, losing tickets stay live and transferable, carry no claim, and can never be burned. How are frontends and indexers meant to present them?

Pointer: the 60 harness-flagged unenforced assumptions are carried verbatim in DOSSIER.md §10.1 and grouped with cross-record notes in §10.2. UA-07 conflicts with DESIGN.md L2's stated independence of sponsor/treasury claims. UA-42 and UA-54 have code paths in the record set where they do not hold (§9.1, §10.2).

logs: Not analyzed (12, ranked below the cut): Raffle.initialize (L176-206), Raffle._transferQuote (L564-567), Raffle._requireWinningTicket (L579-585), Raffle.releaseSponsorProceeds (L375-382), Raffle.releaseProtocolFees (L385-392), RaffleFactory._validateCreateParams (L154-179), VRFV2PlusWrapperConsumerBase.rawFulfillRandomWords (Chainlink L101-107), Raffle constructor (L155-166) and _validatedVrfWrapper (L610-613), RaffleFactory constructor (L65-92), Raffle.callbackDeadline (L463-465), Raffle.drawRequestDeadline (L458-460), VRFV2PlusWrapperConsumerBase.requestRandomnessPayInNative (Chainlink L76-87)
summary: Build an audit context dossier: orient, analyze each function to disk, synthesize a system model

phases.title: Orient
phases.detail: map modules, entrypoints, actors, state; rank functions worth depth

phases.title: Analyze
